title: Cartesian pushout products of inner anodyne maps
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use simplicial sets and inner horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. An inner fibration is a simplicial map having the right lifting property against every inner horn inclusion. A simplicial map is inner anodyne if it has the left lifting property against every inner fibration; a lifting property means the existence of a diagonal filling each commutative square. Let $i:A\to B$ be inner anodyne and let $j:C\to D$ be degreewise injective. Then the cartesian pushout-product map
$$ (A\times D)\amalg_{A\times C}(B\times C)\longrightarrow B\times D $$
is inner anodyne. The products and the pushout here are computed degreewise in sets.

SSet has the degreewise cartesian monoidal structure (same file lines 19-29); innerAnodyneExtensions is innerFibrations.llp in Inner/Basic.lean:43 and innerFibrations is innerHornInclusions.rlp in Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/Quasicategory/InnerFibration.lean:64. This is precisely the statement’s lifting-class convention. Degreewise injectivity supplies Mono j directly: if two simplicial maps become equal after composition with j, cancel the injective j in each degree. No non-elementary comparison of notions is needed.
